questions.question: Which one is a stative verb?
questions.explanation: Stative verbs describe a state, not an action, and are not used in continuous tense. Groups: emotion (love, hate), possession (have, own, belong), sense (see, hear, smell).

questions.question: I shall meet my friend when _____.
questions.explanation: When two future actions are joined by "when": the "when" clause uses Present Indefinite, the main clause uses Future Indefinite. → "when he comes".

questions.question: When I ___ money, I will buy a dictionary.
questions.explanation: "When" clause for future → Present Indefinite. "When I get money, I will buy a dictionary."

questions.question: The ring that I was looking at is gone, someone else ___ it.
questions.explanation: To express a certain inference about past action: must have + V3. → "someone else must have bought it".

questions.question: We _____ to Dhaka just a few months ago.
questions.explanation: Time expressions like "ago", "yesterday", "last month" → Past Indefinite tense. → "We moved to Dhaka just a few months ago."

questions.question: The past participle form of the verb 'Fell' is-
questions.explanation: "Fell" (to knock down) → past: fell, past participle: felled. Note: "Fall" (to drop) → fell → fallen.

questions.question: Which of the following is a strong verb?
questions.explanation: Strong/Irregular verbs change their internal vowel: Run – Ran – Run. Weak/Regular verbs add -d/-ed/-t: Walk – Walked – Walked.

questions.question: I waited for my friend until he_______.
questions.explanation: Sequence of tense: first clause is Past Indefinite → following clause must also be Past Indefinite. → "until he came".

questions.question: Rina proceeded as though she (know) everything.
questions.explanation: "as if/as though" with Past Simple main clause → Past Perfect in subordinate clause. → "as though she had known everything."

questions.question: He expressed his opinion in a way as if he _______ a PhD in the subject.
questions.explanation: Main clause in Past Indefinite + "as if/as though" → subordinate clause uses Past Perfect. → "as if he had done a PhD".

questions.question: I opened the door as soon as I _______ the bell.
questions.explanation: Both clauses are about past events in sequence. "as soon as" joins two Past Simple actions. → "as soon as I heard the bell."

questions.question: The example of present progressive is-
questions.explanation: Present Progressive/Continuous: Subject + am/is/are + verb-ing. → "They are gossiping."

questions.question: How much did you_______ the book?
questions.explanation: "Pay for" is the correct collocation when expressing the price paid for something. → "How much did you pay for the book?"

questions.question: By the middle of the twenty-first century, the computer _____ a necessity in every home.
questions.explanation: "By + future time" → Future Perfect tense: will/shall + have + V3. → "will have become".

questions.question: I could not do it until ten minutes _____ over.
questions.explanation: "Until" joining two past actions where one completes before the other → Past Perfect. → "until ten minutes had been over."

questions.question: It is many years since I _____ there.
questions.explanation: "Since" with Present Indefinite/Present Perfect in first clause → Past Indefinite in following clause. → "since I went there."

questions.question: We _____ for the bus before we decided to walk.
questions.explanation: An action that was ongoing before another past action → Past Perfect Continuous: had been + V-ing. → "We had been waiting for the bus before we decided to walk."

questions.question: I _______ the work before I leave my office.
questions.explanation: One future action completed before another → Future Perfect: shall/will + have + V3. → "I shall have finished the work before I leave."

questions.question: Had the media exposed the government's plans, the genocide ___________________.
questions.explanation: Third conditional (unreal past) structure: Had + subject + V3, subject + might/would + have + V3. 'Might not have occurred' is correct.
